newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas futures end with cold weather gains.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas futures end with cold weather gains.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended broadly higher Tuesday in a sluggish, pre-holiday session, still supported by concerns about low inventories and forecasts for more below-normal weather next week.
January climbed 8.7 cents to close at $3.581 per million British thermal units. February settled 7.1 cents higher at $3.117. Other months ended up by 2.3 to 8.5 cents.

"Weather and storage are still hyping the market, but it feels overdone, and if it doesn't get cold, you could see it dump," said one East Coast trader, noting early-December Gulf cash was holding on the cold weather forecasts.

With overall stocks still 181 bcf, or six percent, below year-ago and supportive weather on the near-term horizon, most expected cash and futures to hold near current levels when December flows begin.
A preliminary Reuter poll for Wednesday's weekly AGA stock report showed expectations for a draw ranged from 60 to 97 bcf. For the same week last year, stocks fell by 61 bcf.
NYMEX will be closed Thursday and Friday for the U.S. Thanksgiving Day holiday.
Technical traders still pegged January support in the mid-$3.20s and then at $3.04. Resistance remained at the $3.68 contract high.

Cash sources said November Gulf Coast gas firmed by 15-20 cents Tuesday to the high-$3.80s, with December on the same pipes notionally little changed in the low-to-mid $3.80s. November Midwest prices were steady to down slightly at about $3.80, with December notionally unchanged to lower at $3.80. December gas at the New York city gate was thinly talked around $5.00.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip rose 6.5 cents to $2.514. NYMEX said 23,808 Hub contracts traded, up from Monday's revised tally of 22,698.
NYMEX Alberta natgas was untraded Tuesday, with January settling unchanged at $1.95.
NYMEX Permian natgas also did not trade. January closed unchanged at $3.15.

On the KCBT, January finished up 10 cents at a new contract high of $3.37, while forward months ended one to eight cents higher. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.3 cents to 21.1 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 199 contracts traded, down from Monday's total of 349.
